Rachel / Lauren / Samir — quick technical readout from the CSV and initial sizing assumptions: 

Findings from the sample:
- Baseline steady-state: ~18 QPS * 400 avg tokens = ~7,200 tokens/sec sustained.
- Peak bursts: sustained 7–12 minutes at ~180 QPS with avg 1,800 tokens = ~324,000 tokens/sec during peak fan-outs. (These are the rows Samir labeled as "analytics_burst".)
- Nightly batch: lower concurrency but very large tokens/request (avg 5k) — we model as throughput-heavy but latency-tolerant.

Preliminary sizing (ballpark):
- Option A (single high-capacity): To hit peak without fallbacks we estimate needing ~4 x A100-class allocations with optimized kernel set and continuous batching to keep P95(streaming) ~250–300ms. This assumes 60–70% KV cache hit rate for repeated context; with cold cache P95 will increase ~1.4x.
- Option B (multi-tier): Keep steady on Hosted medium instances sized for 7,200 tokens/sec (~1 x A100 or equivalent), route 95% of burst traffic to a dedicated burst pool composed of 8 x smaller T4-like nodes running quantized variants; expect P95(streaming) ~320–420ms on the burst pool but cost ~35% lower during sustained bursts. Fallback policy: if burst pool utilization >85% then start routing low-priority batched jobs to a queued worker with best-effort latency SLAs.

Concurrency notes & streaming:
- For ~80 concurrent streaming UI sessions at peak, recommend per-instance session multiplexing with KV sharding to avoid KV contention.
- Suggest pre-warming for the analytics jobs: start 60s before expected fan-out; warmup drastically reduces tail.

Ask for Samir: can you share a short sample of KV cache key reuse (example request ids) so we can estimate realistic hit rates? Also any SLA flex (e.g., allowed P95 uplift during bursts) will change recommended hardware.

I'll draft the numeric table (tokens/sec -> GPU count, per-minute cost projection) and drop into a short PDF for Rachel to circulate.

Dylan
